about.title: Mijung IM
about.subtitle: Pianist of Peace & Nature
about.quoteText: One of the most important pianists of our time.
about.quoteAttribution: Maurice Hinson, American pianist, pedagogue, and critic
about.bioMedium:
Mijung IM is an internationally acclaimed concert pianist known as the Pianist of Peace & Nature. Her performances are distinguished by clarity of tone, contemplative depth, and spiritual artistry. Through her artistry, she explores music as a meeting place of sound, silence, and human presence, inviting listeners into a deeper awareness of our shared humanity.

She serves as Professor of Music at Hansei University in Korea. A graduate of Seoul National University, she earned her Master's degree from The Juilliard School, her Doctor of Musical Arts degree from Stony Brook University, and later a Master's degree in Life Culture Studies from The Catholic University of Korea. She won First Prize at the Dong-A Music Competition (1984) and the San Antonio International Piano Competition (1997, now The Gurwitz International Piano Competition), launching an international performing career.

Im has appeared as soloist and recitalist throughout the United States, Europe, and Asia, including appearances at David Geffen Hall at Lincoln Center and other major venues across New York, Chicago, Washington, D.C., Austria, Hungary, Bulgaria, Switzerland, and numerous cities throughout China. The late American pianist, pedagogue, and critic Maurice Hinson described her as "one of the most important pianists of our time."

Beyond the concert stage, Im has expanded the artistic role of classical music through education, cultural exchange, and projects that foster peace. In 2005, she founded Music for One, a nonprofit organization through which she began developing initiatives that connect music with education, cultural dialogue, and peace. That same year, she presented One Nation: From Jeju to Pyongyang, a recital project symbolically connecting the southernmost and northernmost regions of the Korean Peninsula through music. Her educational initiatives have since extended to Cambodia, Myanmar, Tanzania, and India through music education, online learning, and youth music programs. From 2019, she served as Artistic Director of the PLZ (Peace & Life Zone) Festival in Korea's DMZ border region and later as General Director of the DMZ OPEN International Music Festival (2023–2024). In July 2023, a photograph of her performance at the PLZ Festival was featured on the cover of The New York Times. Through her performances, teaching, and artistic leadership, she continues to explore music as a living art that unites technical excellence with spiritual depth, inviting audiences into a deeper awareness of our shared humanity.

performances.subtitle: Selected engagements, concert archive, and repertoire
performances.headerStatement:
Every performance is an invitation to enter the music's own sense of time.

Listening becomes an act of presence, where sound, silence, and resonance unfold with quiet clarity.

Within that shared moment, music reveals its inner life—awakening a deeper awareness of ourselves, one another, and the mystery that quietly connects us.

projects.title: Projects
projects.subtitle: Festivals, foundations, and educational initiatives
projects.plzBody: Founded in 2019 with the support of Gangwon Province, the PLZ Festival reimagines Korea's DMZ border region not only as a symbol of division, but as a Peace and Life Zone. Under Mijung IM's artistic direction, performances were created in railway stations, beaches, forests, churches, botanical gardens, and historic locations.
projects.plzImageCaption: Mijung IM performing on the shore of Korea's East Sea
projects.dmzBody: Appointed as General Director of Gyeonggi Province's DMZ OPEN Festival, Mijung IM curated and led its International Music Festival, bringing together distinguished soloists, major orchestras, and laureates of leading international competitions.
projects.foundationBody: Founded by Mijung IM in 2005, the Music for One Foundation develops artistic and educational programs that connect music with dignity, cultural dialogue, and human development. Its initiatives have included music education and international exchange projects in Cambodia, Myanmar, Tanzania, and India.

home.statementHeadline: Her performances unite technical excellence with contemplative depth.
home.statementTagline: Where music meets silence, nature, and human presence.
home.introBody: Some performances are remembered for their virtuosity. Others remain with us because of the place they create within the listener. Pianist Mijung IM brings these two dimensions together. Her playing combines clarity of tone, technical command, contemplative depth, and a deeply personal sense of musical presence. Whether performing in an established concert hall or in a landscape shaped by history, she approaches music as a living encounter—between sound and silence, memory and hope, the individual and the wider human experience. Through a career spanning the United States, Europe, and Asia, she has developed an artistic identity that is both classically grounded and unmistakably her own.
